about: Paper of the week for valentynakundas.github.io. `weeks` holds one entry per Monday (ISO date, YYYY-MM-DD). The page shows the latest entry whose week is on or before today and lists the rest as an archive. Every entry must be a peer-reviewed paper published within the last ~2 months of the week it is posted, with a DOI verified against Crossref. `classics` is a reference list of older foundational papers; it is NOT scheduled by the routine.

weeks.title: Increased dependencies among plant performance traits, root exudates and the rhizosphere microbiome under drought
weeks.authors: Judith R. Schepers, Jan Waelchli, Axel Birkholz, Jessica Heblack, Klaus Schlaeppi, Yvonne Willi
weeks.summary: The authors grew Arabidopsis lyrata under drought and well-watered conditions, measured root exudates by gas chromatography, sequenced the rhizosphere bacteria and fungi, and recorded plant performance traits such as biomass and flowering. They then used network analysis to ask whether the links among traits, exudate compounds and microbes tighten under drought. Drought changed the exudate composition and the rhizosphere bacteria, but not the fungi. The drought networks were more connected than the well-watered ones, meaning more associations among performance traits, exudates and rhizosphere taxa, and several performance traits correlated positively with known plant-growth-promoting bacteria. The authors read this as stressed plants relying more on their rhizosphere microbiome.
weeks.why: This is your water treatment, measured from three sides at once: plant traits, what the roots release, and who is in the rhizosphere. Two things to take from it. First, the bacteria moved under drought while the fungi did not, which supports focusing your 16S work on bacteria and gives you a published comparison when you explain that choice. Second, the network approach is a way to show that drought changes relationships, not only abundances, and it would work with your biomass, tissue moisture, WinRHIZO and sequencing data on the same pots. Note that they had no light treatment, so your light-by-water design can ask whether the tighter connections they saw under drought survive when light is also limiting.

weeks.title: Sucrose and pipecolic acid-mediated enrichment of rhizosphere Rhizobiale Burkholderiale bacteria improve soybean growth under low light conditions
weeks.authors: Dongmei Li, Chunting Zhang, Wenqian Wang, Luming Ma, Yaru Huang, Liang Liu, Jinshui Yang, Entao Wang, Feng Jiang, Hongli Yuan
weeks.summary: The authors asked how low light changes the soybean rhizosphere microbiome and whether the bacteria can buffer the damage. A meta-analysis of field studies showed that light intensity was the main driver of yield loss in intercropped and densely planted legumes. In pots, low light suppressed photosynthesis, biomass and nodulation, and the damage was worse in sterile soil. Soil conditioned by low-light plants reduced the growth of the next plants grown in it. Low light made rhizosphere assembly more deterministic, lowered bacterial diversity, simplified co-occurrence networks, and depleted Rhizobiales and Burkholderiales. Sucrose and pipecolic acid in the exudates tracked these taxa, and both attracted the bacteria in chemotaxis assays. Adding back isolates or a simplified synthetic community restored much of the growth lost under low light.
weeks.why: This is the closest published match to your light cycles. It is a legume, the treatment is low light, the plants are also grown in sterile soil, and the soil-conditioning experiment is the same logic as your transfer design: does a microbiome shaped by a stressed plant change the next plant. Their result says yes, and in the harmful direction, which is a prediction you can test with your light-limited lines. The depletion of Rhizobiales under low light is directly relevant to nodulation by Sinorhizobium in your alfalfa, so worth checking in your 16S data. Their intercropping framing also maps onto your alfalfa-plus-timothy treatment, where shading by the grass is part of what the alfalfa experiences. Finally, the isolate and synthetic community add-back is a model for the functional validation you have asked about.

classics.title: Successive passaging of a plant-associated microbiome reveals robust habitat and host genotype-dependent selection
classics.authors: Norma M. Morella, Francis Cheng-Hsuan Weng, Pierre M. Joubert, C. Jessica E. Metcalf, Steven Lindow, Britt Koskella
classics.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
classics.angle: Tomato phyllosphere passaged over four generations; strong host-genotype and habitat selection, community converges; directly comparable to a four-cycle rhizosphere transfer design.

classics.title: Engineering Microbiomes to Improve Plant and Animal Health
classics.authors: Ulrich G. Mueller, Joel L. Sachs
classics.angle: The theory behind host-mediated microbiome selection: what is actually being selected, heritability of a microbiome, and why indirect selection through the host can work.

classics.title: Host-mediated microbiome engineering (HMME) of drought tolerance in the wheat rhizosphere
classics.authors: Michael D. Jochum, Kelsey L. McWilliams, Elizabeth A. Pierson, Young-Ki Jo
classics.angle: Closest analogue to selecting a rhizosphere microbiome for drought tolerance; note how they defined drought, how many rounds, and what changed in the community.

classics.title: Drought delays development of the sorghum root microbiome and enriches for monoderm bacteria
classics.authors: Ling Xu, Dan Naylor, Zhaobin Dong, Tuesday Simmons, Grady Pierroz, Kim K. Hixson, Young-Mo Kim, Erika M. Zink, Kristin M. Engbrecht, Yi Wang, Cheng Gao, Stephanie DeGraaf, Mary A. Madera, Julie A. Sievert, Joy Hollingsworth, Devin Birdseye, Henrik V. Scheller, Robert Hutmacher, Jeffery Dahlberg, Christer Jansson, Susannah G. Tringe, Jeffery A. Dahlberg, Peggy G. Lemaux, Devin Coleman-Derr
classics.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
classics.angle: What drought does to a root microbiome over time: monoderm (Actinobacteria) enrichment, delayed assembly, reversal after rewatering; gives expected taxa to look for in drought treatments.

classics.title: Drought Stress and Root-Associated Bacterial Communities
classics.authors: Dan Naylor, Devin Coleman-Derr
classics.angle: Review framework for drought and root bacteria: direct effects on bacteria versus effects routed through the plant.

classics.title: Life in Dry Soils: Effects of Drought on Soil Microbial Communities and Processes
classics.authors: Joshua P. Schimel
classics.journal: Annual Review of Ecology, Evolution, and Systematics
classics.angle: Soil water physics for microbiologists: water potential versus water content, why percent water-holding capacity is not the quantity bacteria experience, and how to report drought treatments physically.

classics.title: Plant root exudation under drought: implications for ecosystem functioning
classics.authors: Alex Williams, Franciska T. de Vries
classics.angle: How drought changes what roots release and therefore what the rhizosphere bacteria are fed; the link between a shoot-level treatment and a root-level microbiome response.

classics.title: Drought-induced recruitment of specific root-associated bacteria enhances adaptation of alfalfa to drought stress
classics.authors: Wenqiang Fan, Fang Tang, Jiani Wang, Jiaqi Dong, Jing Xing, Fengling Shi
classics.angle: Alfalfa specifically: which root-associated bacteria drought recruits and whether they help; a direct comparison set for the alfalfa treatments.

classics.title: The plant circadian clock influences rhizosphere community structure and function
classics.authors: Charley J. Hubbard, Marcus T. Brock, Linda T. A. van Diepen, Loïs Maignien, Brent E. Ewers, Cynthia Weinig
classics.angle: Evidence that the plant's light-driven clock shapes the rhizosphere; the mechanistic reason a photoperiod treatment can move the microbiome at all.

classics.title: Stress combination: from genes to ecosystems
classics.authors: Sara I. Zandalinas, Jorge J. Casal, Hatem Rouached, Ron Mittler
classics.angle: Why combined stresses are not additive and how to design and interpret a factorial stress experiment; the conceptual backbone for the light-by-water design.

classics.title: Soil microbiome transfer method affects microbiome composition, including dominant microorganisms, in a novel environment
classics.authors: Mia M. Howard, Terrence H. Bell, Jenny Kao-Kniffin
classics.angle: From the lab: how the way you transfer a microbiome into sterilized soil changes what establishes; directly about the transfer step in each cycle.

classics.title: Microbiome Datasets Are Compositional: And This Is Not Optional
classics.authors: Gregory B. Gloor, Jean M. Macklaim, Vera Pawlowsky-Glahn, Juan J. Egozcue
classics.angle: Why relative-abundance tables need compositional methods (CLR, Aitchison distance) and what goes wrong with Bray-Curtis and differential abundance on raw proportions.

classics.title: Pseudoreplication and the Design of Ecological Field Experiments
classics.authors: Stuart H. Hurlbert
classics.angle: The classic on experimental units: why the pot, not the plant, is the replicate, and how to say so in a thesis.

classics.title: Lucerne (Medicago sativa) alters N2O-reducing communities associated with cocksfoot (Dactylis glomerata) roots
classics.authors: Daniel R. H. Graf, Aurélien Saghaï, Jun Zhao, Georg Carlsson, Christopher M. Jones, Sara Hallin
classics.angle: Alfalfa grown with a grass changes the grass's root bacteria; the reference point for the alfalfa-plus-timothy treatment.

classics.title: The Inherent Conflicts in Developing Soil Microbial Inoculants
classics.authors: Laura M. Kaminsky, Ryan V. Trexler, Rondy J. Malik, Kevin L. Hockett, Terrence H. Bell
classics.angle: From the lab: why a selected or engineered microbiome struggles once it leaves sterile soil; frames the translation question for the discussion chapter.

classics.title: Harnessing rhizosphere microbiomes for drought-resilient crop production
classics.authors: Franciska T. de Vries, Rob I. Griffiths, Christopher G. Knight, Oceane Nicolitch, Alex Williams
classics.angle: The big-picture review of drought, roots and rhizosphere bacteria; useful for the introduction and for placing microbiome selection among other approaches.

classics.title: Assembly and ecological function of the root microbiome across angiosperm plant species
classics.authors: Connor R. Fitzpatrick, Julia Copeland, Pauline W. Wang, David S. Guttman, Peter M. Kotanen, Marc T. J. Johnson
classics.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
classics.angle: Thirty plant species under drought in one design; shows how much of the root microbiome is host-specific versus drought-driven, with Streptomyces as a recurring drought taxon.

classics.title: Root exudate metabolomes change under drought and show limited capacity for recovery
classics.authors: Albert Gargallo-Garriga, Catherine Preece, Jordi Sardans, Michal Oravec, Otmar Urban, Josep Peñuelas
classics.angle: Measured exudate chemistry under drought and after rewatering; evidence that the plant-side signal to the rhizosphere does not simply bounce back.

classics.title: A dynamic rhizosphere interplay between tree roots and soil bacteria under drought stress
classics.authors: Yaara Oppenheimer-Shaanan, Gilad Jakoby, Maya L. Starr, Romiel Karliner, Gal Eilon, Sagi Peled, Itamar Shani, Tamir Klein
classics.angle: Roots and bacteria exchanging carbon and water during drought, measured directly; a mechanistic story for how a stressed plant and its bacteria trade.

classics.title: Manipulating Wild and Tamed Phytobiomes: Challenges and Opportunities
classics.authors: Terrence H. Bell, Kevin L. Hockett, Ricky I. Alcalá-Briseño, Mary Barbercheck, Gwyn A. Beattie, Mary Ann Bruns, John E. Carlson, Taejung Chung, Alyssa Collins, Bryan Emmett, Paolo Gugino, Maria del Mar Jiménez-Gasco, Ryan Kaye, Christopher Kiflemariam, Jonathan Kloepper, ...
classics.angle: The lab's position paper on manipulating phytobiomes; a map of where microbiome selection sits and the vocabulary the field uses.

classics.title: Conditioning the soil microbiome through plant–soil feedbacks suppresses an aboveground insect pest
classics.authors: Ana Pineda, Ian Kaplan, S. Emilia Hannula, Wadih Ghanem, T. Martijn Bezemer
classics.angle: Using one plant generation to condition soil that then changes the next plant's outcome; the plant-soil feedback view of the same transfer logic.

classics.title: Light–Root Microbiome Interactions in Vegetable Crops: From Photoreceptor Signaling to Exudate-Mediated Recruitment
classics.authors: Lidiia S. Samarina, Arysgul Turbekova, Daniyar Jantassov, Nurgul Demir, Ruslan Kalendar
classics.angle: Recent review of how light intensity and spectrum reach the root microbiome through photoreceptors and exudates; background for the light treatment.

classics.title: Construction of Drought-Resistant Microbial Consortium and Effect on Alfalfa Growth Under Drought Stress
classics.authors: Xiaolei Yang, Qi Li, et al.
classics.angle: Recent alfalfa drought paper using a designed consortium rather than selection; a contrast for the discussion.
